children: Evommune said its Phase 2b trial of a treatment for people with atopic dermatitis failed to meet its primary and secondary endpoints.
The stock dropped 32%, to $8.95, in after-hours trading Tuesday. Through the close, it was down 24% this year.

The trial was evaluating the efficacy and safety of EVO756, an oral drug meant to treat people with the condition that causes dry, itchy skin. Based on the results, Evommune doesn't plan to advance EVO756 for atopic dermatitis.
The trial enrolled 121 adults with the condition over a 12-week treatment period, with follow-up at week 14.
The treatment was well tolerated for safety, supporting its continued evaluation for migraine prophylaxis.
